 BLG Viper: Historic Win Over T1 “Feels Like a Dream”
 Davide "Dovi" Xu

 A historic win for Bilibili Gaming and the LPL. After losing 13 times on the Worlds stage to T1, the Chinese team has managed to take down the Worlds 2025 champions, avenging the loss in the grand final in 2024.
 It was a monumental series for everyone, including BLG Viper, who now has the chance to become a two-time world champion. If he does, both titles will have come with teams other than T1, a legacy that could put him among the greatest ADCs in League history.
 Following the win, we spoke to Viper about his team, his mentality, and approach as he will play Gen.G in the grand final this Saturday, November 14, in New York.
 Photo Credit: Hotspawn/Riot Games 
 Davide : First of all, that was such a great series.
 How do you feel about getting another win against an LCK team?
 Viper : It feels really good. I still can’t quite believe it, because this is the first time an LPL team has beaten T1 in a best-of-five at Worlds. It feels like a dream.
 Davide : Do you think you’re the best Ezreal in the world?
 Viper : Yeah, I’m the best in the world. I think I’m the best Ezreal in the world, as you can see.
 Davide : What about Ashe?
 Viper : Ashe? I don’t know [about] Ashe… I’m not [as] confident on her.
 Davide : BLG has had its ups and downs this season, but you’ve still made it to every international event and every international final.
 What has this year taught you, and what makes this BLG roster special?
 Viper : Let me think… At our first international event, we made it to the First Stand final against G2 . That success taught us that we’re really good and strong, but we can still lose because we have mistakes and weaknesses. Our opponents can figure out our bad habits.
 At MSI, our opponents did a really good job against us. I believe we’re strong enough to compete at every international event, but we’re also aware that we can make mistakes, sometimes big ones.
 Controlling ourselves is the most important thing for BLG this year.
Discipline is the most important thing. 
 THE CURSE HAS BEEN BROKEN. pic.twitter.com/48Miw3bMx4 
 — LoL Esports (@lolesports) November 9, 2026 
 Davide : Going back in time, before the trophies and everything that came with esports,
 What memory comes to mind when you think about what first got you hooked on League?
 Viper : It’s a simple answer. When I first played the game, I played Blitzcrank. It was a really good experience because I played with my friends. They recommended this new game that had just come out and asked if we wanted to play a game or two at an internet café. We played together, and I thought it was really fun.
 Davide : Did you enjoy playing as a group, with everyone together?
 Viper : Yeah, playing together is more fun. But everyone has their own schedule, so sometimes I have to play alone. That’s okay, because the game is still really fun.
 Is competition something that pushes you forward?
 Viper : Yeah. I really wanted to win because I knew I was good at the game. I thought that if I kept going, I could reach the top of the rankings. So I kept pushing myself, and sometimes I encouraged my friends to play better, too.
 Image Credit: Riot Games 
 Davide : You’ve said that one reason you love esports is that you get to meet new people and have new experiences.
 Is there a particular person or moment that made your career more meaningful in a way you didn’t expect?
 Viper : That’s a good question. A lot of people have helped me. When I first became a pro, in 2018 or 2019, I thought I was the best and that other people weren’t very important. I focused on doing my job well and only cared about myself. At the time, I thought that was okay.
 But after I won Worlds in Iceland in 2021, I realized I couldn’t do it alone. I needed my friends and teammates, and I needed help from other people. That was the biggest change in my life. 
 Davide : In any competitive discipline, people sometimes talk about entering “the zone,” a state of flow where you’re not consciously thinking through everything and can rely on instinct.
 Was there a match or a period in your career when you felt you were playing at your absolute best?
 Viper : The whole 2021 season . At that time, I felt like I didn’t need to do anything else. I could just sit down and play, and I was really good. I felt like I was the best. It didn’t matter who I played against. I just focused and concentrated. I could think about how to avoid an ability, like Malphite’s ultimate, and then do it.
 Whether I was scrimming or playing solo queue, I could just play, and everything would happen the way I expected. I felt like I was processing things step by step, and they would work out as I thought they would. I wasn’t trying to get into the zone; I was already there, especially throughout 2021.
 Image Credit: Riot Games 
 Davide : I’ve always admired you, going back to your Griffin days . I’ve seen you as a complete, well-rounded player who can adapt to different champions, drafts, and playstyles.
 Do you consider yourself a perfectionist? Is that desire to keep improving something you developed through competition, or did you already have it before you became a pro?
 Viper : It’s still hard to explain, but even before I went pro, there were already so many pros in the scene. I wanted to stand out and specialize in something that made me different.
 I thought that if I knew everything about the game, I might be able to get ahead of everyone else and have an advantage. 
 Since I was young, I wasn’t picky. I played every champion and every role: top, mid, jungle, bot, and support. A lot of my League memories come from playing all of those things. Besides scrimming and practicing, I was able to play what I wanted, and I think that helped me stay a step ahead of other players. Maybe I already had that desire to get ahead and become a standout player in me.
 As for being a perfectionist, I do pursue perfection, even though I know it’s impossible . I do everything I can to become the perfect player. I used to think I could make it through playoffs without dropping a single game, but losses are sometimes unavoidable in competition.
 Luck can be part of it, too, as much as I hate to say that. I keep thinking about what I can do as a player and what else I can contribute to help the team win. That’s what I always strive for.
 Davide : That’s a lovely answer. Thank you very much, Viper, and good luck in the Grand Final next week in New York.
 If you enjoyed our interview, follow our Worlds 2026 coverage and check out our social media channels for more exclusive content!
